title: Heaviest box per shelf
scenario: For each shelf, its single heaviest box.

intro.job: For each shelf, its single heaviest box.

idea.rule: max(shelves) looks at the OUTER box — the shelf names. max(shelves[name]) opens that shelf's box of weights first.
idea.detail: shelves is a dict whose values are lists. shelves['a'] opens the outer box and hands you a's list [2, 9, 4]; one more step — max(...) — reaches into that list. Each pair of brackets opens one more box, so say what's in your hand after each one.

model_restatement: For every shelf, find the largest weight in its list of boxes.

clarify.question: Could a shelf have no boxes?
clarify.answer: Not today — every shelf has at least one.

clarify.question: What if two boxes tie for heaviest?
What shape should the answer be?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: For each shelf, take the biggest of the boxes. Put it in a dict. Print it.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after iteration 1, what is heaviest?

why_line: max(shelves) is handed the whole dict of shelves — and max of a dict looks at its keys, so it picks the biggest NAME, 'b', not a weight.

explain.rule: max(shelves) reaches into the wrong box: it opens the box of shelves and picks the biggest name tag — 'b' — instead of opening a's box of weights.
explain.bridge: So which box should max be handed — the box of shelves, or a's box of boxes?

fix.rule: max(shelves[name]): open the shelf's box, then hand the whole list to max.

walk.gloss: An empty dict for the answers.
Open their list of boxes and keep the heaviest.

alternatives.code: print({name: max(weights) for name, weights in shelves.items()})

hints: After iteration 1, did a get a weight — or a name?
max(shelves) looks at the dict's keys — the shelf names. Open this shelf's box first.

follow_up.prompt: One shelf, one box: {'z': [6]} — what's printed?

checkpoint.prompt: With the new shelves, what gets printed?

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — max still finds the heaviest.

one_liner: max(shelves) looks at the OUTER box — the shelf names. max(shelves[name]) opens that shelf's box of weights first.
